plants.name: Hippeastrum hybrids
plants.description: Towering trumpet-shaped blooms in rich shades of red, white and pink open atop sturdy, leafless stalks. Gardeners in the Southern Hemisphere see them flower outdoors in the warmth of midsummer. Elsewhere, they are a familiar sight on windowsills during the winter holidays.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere: late spring to midsummer (roughly November to January). Indoors in the Northern Hemisphere: winter, usually December to February.
plants.location: Gardens in Australia, New Zealand and South Africa, and indoor displays across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Amaryllis bulbs store so much energy that a single bulb can send up a flower stalk that grows several inches in just a few days.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Round clusters of blue-violet, funnel-shaped flowers sway on tall stems above arching, strap-like leaves. In midsummer they fill Southern Hemisphere gardens and roadsides with waves of color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, roughly December to February
plants.location: Native to South Africa's Eastern Cape; widely grown in Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Its name comes from the Greek words for 'love' and 'flower'. Despite the common name, it is not a true lily.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs are covered in rose-like blossoms in the cool months. The blooms stand out against dark green leaves, adding color to winter gardens in mild climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, with many varieties in flower in December and January
plants.location: Gardens in the southeastern United States, the Pacific coast of North America, western Europe and Japan
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Both belong to the same genus.
